old_value: Often brambly and strongly spiced, with old vines giving small berries and concentrated flavor.
reason: Sonoma County Winegrowers supports small berries and intensity of flavour from old vines and pronounced spice (Santa Rosa Plain sites only); it does not say brambly. Both Wine Enthusiast pages return 403 and could not be checked, and they are single wine reviews from Dry Creek Valley, not a description of Sonoma County Zinfandel. Only one source verified.

old_value: Tighter and more structured than North Island Pinot Gris, with a pure and lively feel.
reason: Wine Companion supports tighter and more structured than North Island Pinot Gris. NZ Wine only says Riesling, Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer reflect the region's purity and vivacity. Each half rests on one source.

old_value: Pure and lively, with citrus fruit, turning honeyed in late harvest styles.
reason: Wine Companion supports lemon and lime and honeyed late harvest styles; NZ Wine supports only purity and vivacity (shared with Pinot Gris and Gewurztraminer). Citrus and honeyed late harvest rest on one source.

old_value: Bright and vivid, made in every style from dry to sweet.
reason: NZ Wine supports bright, vivid and dry to dessert styles. Decanter page truncated on fetch, text not verifiable. Wine Companion Canterbury page has no North Canterbury Riesling description; search found only producer and retailer pages.

old_value: Crisp and mineral, often with a flinty edge.
reason: Wine Anorak: Constantia known for crisp, fresh whites (not Sauvignon Blanc specific; no mineral or flinty). Decanter: one Klein Constantia wine, mineral and flinty. No claim has two sources for Constantia Sauvignon Blanc as a whole.

old_value: Rich and textured with a waxy, lanolin feel, yet still fresh.
reason: WOSA (quoting a producer) supports waxy lanolin texture; does not say rich or fresh. Wine Anorak is a single wine note (wax, textured, rich, fresh). Jancis Robinson South African Semillon article returned 403. Close: if a single wine note may count, "Textured, with a waxy, lanolin feel" would hold.

old_value: Elegant and restrained, with a firm, almost austere line from cool sites and clay rich soils.
reason: Wine Society supports elegant and restrained (cool valley); no firm, austere or clay. Decanter premium page unreachable (title only). Search found only single wine reviews.

old_value: Perfumed and powerful, with floral and dark spice notes and firm but smooth tannins.
reason: WOSA supports florals, dark spice, perfume, power and firm yet unharsh tannins. Decanter tasting note is paywalled and was a single wine anyway. Only one source verified.

old_value: Dry farmed old vines give concentrated, richly fruited wines that keep their freshness.
reason: Wine Folly says only "richly fruity". Decanter premium page unreachable. Wine Society says Swartland has some of the best old Chenin vines but nothing on dry farming, concentration or freshness.

old_value: Grown on old bush vines and increasingly bottled on its own, as well as used in blends.
reason: Decanter premium page unreachable (title only). Wine Society mentions Cinsault only as a blend partner, not in Swartland, and says nothing of it being bottled on its own.

old_value: Pale, light and fresh, with fine tannins and moderate alcohol.
reason: Decanter premium page unreachable. Winemag note on one Badenhorst Cinsault: light and fresh with fine tannins, but the vineyard origin is not stated; nothing on pale colour or alcohol.

old_value: One of the main white grapes around San Patricio del Chañar, suited to the cool nights of northern Patagonia.
reason: Wines of Argentina sheet confirms Chardonnay among main varieties of Añelo department / San Patricio del Chañar and cold nights in Neuquén. Wine Spectator is Patagonia wide only. One source for the Añelo specific claim.

old_value: Colchagua Cabernet often leans to an elegant style, deep in colour and fresh enough to age well.
reason: Wine Folly: "more elegant, Bordeaux-styled Cabernet" from Colchagua. Wines of Chile: excellent colour, freshness and cellaring said of Colchagua reds in general. Elegant and colour/freshness/ageing each rest on one source.

old_value: The main white grape of the valley, while Syrah leads the reds.
final_value: The main white grape of the valley, while Syrah leads the reds.
reason: Wines of Chile: leading strains are Syrah for reds and Sauvignon Blanc among whites. Second source found: winetourism.com Elqui page, "the most commonly produced wines in the region are Sauvignon Blanc and Syrah". Wine Folly (cited) does not say main grape.

old_value: From these cool, high sites it is leaner and more scented than the plump Syrah of Chile's warm central valleys.
reason: Wine Folly supports lean, peppery Elqui style versus plump Maipo/Colchagua. Wine Society: scented cool climate Syrah from one Falernia vineyard only. Leaner rests on one source; scented on one producer.

old_value: One of the valley's main red grapes, alongside Merlot.
reason: Wines of Chile: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot thrive "as well" (not called main). Wine Folly: look for Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Carignan, no Merlot. Neither says main red grape; Merlot on one source.

old_value: Grauburgunder
reason: Swiss Wine Promotion: called Grauburgunder in German speaking Switzerland. Canton of Graubünden vineyard statistics 2025 list the variety as Grauburgunder throughout (text extracted and checked); cantonal regulation 917.400 also uses "Grau- oder Weissburgunder". Two independent bodies.

old_value: In Neuchâtel, Chasselas is lively and fresh, with a fine mineral edge from the limestone soils.
reason: Swiss Wine Promotion supports lively Chasselas and limestone soils favouring fresh Chasselas in Neuchâtel; says nothing of mineral for Neuchâtel (fine minerality is said of Lake Biel). Hachette has no regional description (its appellation text is a Chablis copy error); only single wine reviews. One source.

old_value: In Badacsony it is lean and sharply acidic when young, with a salty, slightly oily texture, and needs a year or two in bottle to open up.
reason: Wines of Hungary (bor.hu) supports every claim. Badacsony specification: slightly salty notes for Badacsony wines generally, not this grape. Decanter piece is sponsored (sponsor not named, independence unconfirmed) and says crunchy, understated young, honeyed with age; no acidity or salt. No claim has two independent grape specific sources.

old_value: Most Istrian Malvazija is made fresh and young in steel, while skin contact and oak give fuller, more textured and gently honeyed versions.
reason: GuildSomm: styles range from heavily oaked to fresh, young and fruity; no steel, skin contact or honeyed. Decanter guide is produced with Vinistra and the Croatian tourist board, and its Malvazija text was cut off on fetch, so steel, skin contact and honeyed could not be verified.

old_value: Under its Moldovan name it is a typical grape of PGI Ștefan Vodă, where its best known wines come from around Purcari, made on its own and blended with Cabernet Sauvignon and Saperavi in Negru de Purcari.
final_value: A typical grape of PGI Ștefan Vodă, made on its own and blended with Cabernet Sauvignon and Saperavi in Negru de Purcari.
reason: Typical grape: Wine of Moldova Ștefan Vodă page lists Rară Neagră among predominant varieties; winetourism.com names it among typical grapes. Varietal: Wine Anorak (Rară Neagră de Purcari) and Wine of Moldova local varieties page (best wines of the variety from Purcari and other Ștefan Vodă localities). Negru de Purcari blend: Wine Anorak and Decanter review. Trimmed "under its Moldovan name" and "best known wines come from around Purcari" (one source).

old_value: One of the typical grapes of PGI Ștefan Vodă, a region given mainly to red wine, where it is made on its own and leads blends such as Negru de Purcari with Saperavi and Rară Neagră.
final_value: One of the typical grapes of PGI Ștefan Vodă, a region given mainly to red wine, where it is blended with Saperavi and Rară Neagră in Negru de Purcari.
reason: Typical grape and red wine region: winetourism.com ("an absolute red wine region", typical wines from Cabernet Sauvignon) and Wine of Moldova Ștefan Vodă page (predominant varieties, renowned for red wines). Negru de Purcari blend: Wine Anorak and Decanter review. Trimmed "made on its own" (no source shows a varietal from this PGI) and "leads" (interpretive).

old_value: A late ripening grape, it is grown here because the Struma valley is warmer than the rest of Bulgaria, and it is the parent of the earlier ripening Melnik crossings bred for the area.
final_value: The parent of the earlier ripening Melnik crossings, such as Melnik 55.
reason: Wine Anorak: the Melnik "children" were created to be earlier ripening, Shiroka Melnik the parent. Wine Folly: Melnik 55 is a cross of Broad leafed Melnik and Valdiguié. Exotic Wine Travel: late ripening, hence the hybrid. Trimmed late ripening (explicit only in Exotic Wine Travel) and "grown here because the Struma valley is warmer" (Wine Anorak only; Wine Folly calls the area mountainous).

old_value: Bred from Shiroka Melnishka to ripen earlier, it is made here both as a single varietal wine and in blends.
final_value: Bred from Shiroka Melnishka to ripen earlier.
reason: Parentage: Wine Folly and Exotic Wine Travel. Earlier ripening: Wine Anorak and Exotic Wine Travel (hybrid made because the parent ripens late). Single varietal and blends rest on Wine Folly alone, trimmed.

old_value: In the cool mountain vineyards of Aigialeia Roditis ripens slowly into its most aromatic wines, while lower, warmer sites near Patras give fuller, more generous whites.
reason: Wines of Greece supports gentle ripening and most aromatic Roditis in Aigialeia, fuller body near Patras (but says the Patras climate is similar, not warmer). Decanter page truncated on fetch. Wine Anorak (Rouvalis, Aigialeia) says Roditis "isn't very aromatic" and lower vineyards give less flavour, contradicting the claim.

old_value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Syrah and Merlot, and bottled on its own under the Rift Valley label.
final_value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Syrah and Merlot.
reason: Embassy: Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon chosen for the reds at the Ziway vineyard. Winemag: Castel reds from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah (Rift Valley, does not name Ziway). Bottled on its own rests on the embassy alone (Jancis Robinson page 403), trimmed.

old_value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, and bottled on its own under the Rift Valley label.
final_value: One of the three red grapes of the Castel estate near Ziway, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.
reason: Same two sources as Cabernet Sauvignon. No source verified a Rift Valley Syrah bottling (embassy lists Syrah only in the Acacia blend; Jancis Robinson page 403), trimmed.

old_value: In Hokkaido it is crisp and light, with a fresh citrus scent and clear acidity.
reason: GI specification describes Hokkaido whites in general, not Kerner. Ishikari page is one Kerner (refreshing citrus aroma); no crisp, light or acidity. Not two Kerner specific sources.

old_value: Here it gives light, fresh wines with a lemony, citrus edge, most marked when the grapes are picked early.
reason: GI Osaka specification (as cited) supports fresh aroma and citrus when picked early. Wine Anorak is one wine (light, fresh, lemony); early picking not mentioned. Close: holds only if a single wine note counts as second support.

old_value: The region's signature red grape, typically made into structured red wines that can age.
reason: Decanter piece is sponsor content created with Uruguay Wine (INAVI), so effectively one body; it supports champion of the region and structured, ageworthy Tannat. SevenFifty says only that Tannat dominates plantings (a share claim) and nothing of structure or ageing.

old_value: Here the ocean and granite soils give Tannat more freshness and a mineral energy.
final_value: Here Tannat has a mineral character.
reason: World of Fine Wine: "the mineral verve of the Tannat". Wine Folly: Maldonado gives mineral rich, powerful wines, especially Tannat. More freshness rests only on the INAVI sponsored Decanter piece, and the ocean and granite causation is not stated by two sources; trimmed.

old_value: Made dry, off dry and sweet, and with Vidal one of the two main grapes for Icewine.
reason: World of Fine Wine: dry Riesling trend and residual sugar; no Icewine. Wine Country Ontario: majority of Icewine from Riesling and Vidal, Ontario wide. Wine Folly not Canada specific. Niagara specific style range rests on one source; Icewine claim is province wide only.

old_value: Grown for traditional method sparkling wine, often blended with Pinot Noir, as well as for still wines, and allowed as a minor partner in a Tidal Bay blend.
reason: Wines of Nova Scotia article supports Tidal Bay allowing Chardonnay in the up to 49% portion and varietal still Chardonnay (one producer); sparkling text does not name grapes. Wine Anorak covers one producer's traditional method Chardonnay/Pinot Noir. Tourism Nova Scotia page does not list Tidal Bay varieties. Each claim on one source.

old_value: Here it tastes riper and rounder than in the Loire, with cocoa and dried pepper notes over juicy fruit and moderate, smooth tannins.
reason: Wine Folly (Okanagan) supports riper than Loire, cocoa, dried pepper, suede like tannins. GuildSomm describes British Columbia as a whole, not the Okanagan. Wine BC Okanagan page has no matching description.

old_value: Leaner and firmer than most Merlot, with notable tannin and lively natural acidity.
reason: GuildSomm is BC wide. Wine Folly says leaner and fruitier than Bordeaux but nothing on tannin or acidity. Wine BC calls Golden Mile Merlot "plush", which runs against "leaner and firmer".

old_value: Here it is crisp and fresh with high acidity and a lean finish, only turning richer when aged in oak.
reason: Wine Folly (Okanagan): "sky-high acidity, and a lean, tingly finish". Second source found: Wine BC Okanagan page, North Okanagan Riesling, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir "offering vibrant acidity", Golden Mile "preserving acidity and freshness" for Pinot Gris. Crisp, lean finish and oak richness rest on one Okanagan source (GuildSomm is BC wide); trimmed.

old_value: It tends to be fresh and high in acid with firmer tannins than many Pinot Noirs, so it is rarely as light as Burgundy.
final_value: It tends to be high in acid.
reason: Wine Folly (Okanagan): high acidity and crunchy tannins. Wine BC: North Okanagan Pinot Noir with vibrant acidity. Firmer tannins and the Burgundy comparison rest on GuildSomm, which is BC wide; trimmed.

old_value: In Sussex it gives taut, high acid sparkling wine, often described as chalky and mineral, with toast and brioche notes from long ageing on the lees.
reason: Sussex PDO specification (text extracted and checked): crisp acidity from the Chardonnays, brioche and toast from long lees ageing (all sparkling), chalk imparting character (all wines). Wine Folly: Sussex wines chalky, flinty, mineral and acidity preserved, said of the region's wines, not Chardonnay. No Chardonnay specific claim has two sources.
